notes: Read all eight units, full public-banking context, all eight candidates and the review. Split agricultural credit, farmer-debt relief and opposition to corporate concentration. Restored the unified public bank and local community networks as the research-funding mechanism. Split retail account access from monetary accountability. Preserved working-class control as an alternative to breaking up big banks and restored the characterization that capitalist centralization of finance laid the proposal's foundations.

claims.claim_text: The unified public banking system and its local community networks would give farmers affordable credit.
The unified public banking system and its local community networks would relieve farmers' massive debt burdens.
The unified public banking system and its local community networks would fight corporate agricultural concentration.

The unified public banking system and its local community networks would fund nationwide research and development to advance science and reduce university and researcher dependence on Defense Department and corporate contracts.
The unified public banking system and its local community networks would provide dependable savings and checking access in communities underserved by large retail banks.
The unified public banking system and its local community networks would create a more democratically accountable monetary system less influenced by Wall Street and large investment-bank connections.
Capitalism's centralization of finance is characterized as laying foundations for bringing large banks under working-class control for everyone's benefit rather than breaking them up.
